subject.title: Reject split outbound agent session ownership

question: Should OpenClaw deliberately reject explicit-agent and canonical-session owner mismatches, including permanently failing already queued contradictory deliveries, rather than preserving the current explicit-agent precedence?
rationale: The implementation is coherent, but current main intentionally prefers explicit caller ownership and this branch changes that behavior for live and persisted requests; source review cannot establish whether that compatibility break is the intended permanent product contract.

options.title: Adopt fail-closed ownership
options.body: Approve the invariant after current-head proof shows rejection, cross-agent policy-key allowance, and recovery dead-letter behavior.

options.title: Preserve current precedence
options.body: Keep explicit agent ownership for existing requests and narrow any hardening to a separately approved boundary with a defined migration path.

options.title: Defer the contract change
options.body: Pause this PR until outbound and Gateway owners define which canonical session fields may legally cross agent boundaries.

recommendation.title: Adopt fail-closed ownership
recommendation.body: Approve the invariant after current-head proof shows rejection, cross-agent policy-key allowance, and recovery dead-letter behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They were explicitly asked to confirm the outbound/Gateway compatibility contract and have recent adjacent history in outbound and session routing.
